description:
Observer look-angles use the wrong geodetic model, so WGS84 RA/Dec/alt-az come out wrong: the vernal equinox direction should map to RA 0 / Dec 0, the ecliptic north pole to Dec = 90-obliquity, and a meridian body at the observer's declination should sit at the zenith.

## Reporter answers (follow-up)

Q: What specific wrong RA/Dec/alt-az values were observed, and what were the expected correct values? The three provided acceptance criteria all pass, so they don't define what is broken.
A: I don't know.

Q: Was the wrong output observed through a specific consumer (AR sky scene, satellite tracking, something else)?
A: I don't know.

Q: Is the issue about the satellite look-angle pipeline (observerEci spherical Earth) or the astronomy pipeline (ecliptic-to-equatorial conversion, which passes the given tests)?
A: The issue is about the satellite look-angle pipeline. The observer's Earth-centered position used for satellite look-angles is computed on a spherical Earth when it should use the WGS84 ellipsoid with flattening. The spherical-trig alt/az math itself is not the complaint — the observer position model is.

Q: A concrete reproduction: observer location, date/time, target body, observed value, expected value.
A: I don't know.

## Reporter answers (follow-up)

Q: A concrete reference test vector: given a known WGS84 geodetic latitude/longitude and Julian Day, what are the expected observerEci x/y/z coordinates (km) on the ellipsoid surface? The specialist had no oracle to verify the formula was numerically correct — the 'use ellipsoid' criterion describes a mechanism, not a correct output. Need a known-correct triple (lat, lon, jd, x_ref, y_ref, z_ref) from a WGS84 transform implementation or reference table.
A: I don't know.

Q: Optionally, a known-correct alt/az pair for a concrete satellite TLE and observer location/time, to validate the full lookAngle pipeline end-to-end after fixing observerEci. Without this, the specialist can only unit-test the ellipsoid math, not confirm the consumer produces correct results.
A: I don't know.
